Buddy Hield is a Bahamian professional basketball player.
Buddy Hield plays for the Golden State Warriors of the National Basketball Association (NBA).
Buddy Hield played college basketball for the Oklahoma Sooners.
Buddy Hield was named the Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year in 2015 and 2016.
In 2016, Buddy Hield received four major national player of the year awards: the John R. Wooden Award, the Naismith Award, Sporting News Player of the Year, and the Oscar Robertson Trophy.
Buddy Hield was selected with the sixth overall pick in the 2016 NBA draft by the New Orleans Pelicans.
Buddy Hield was traded to the Sacramento Kings for DeMarcus Cousins in 2017.
Buddy Hield was dealt to the Indiana Pacers in a package for Domantas Sabonis in 2022.
In February 2024, Buddy Hield was traded to the Philadelphia 76ers.
In July 2024, Buddy Hield was involved in a 6-team trade that involved him getting traded to the Golden State Warriors.
Buddy Hield grew up in Eight Mile Rock, a coastal region west of Freeport, in the West Grand Bahama district in the Bahamas.
Buddy Hield is the fifth of seven children of his mother Jackie Braynen.
Buddy Hield received his nickname from his mother after Bud Bundy of the sitcom Married... with Children.
Buddy Hield attended Jack Hayward High School in Freeport.
Buddy Hield was first featured in high school by The All Bahamian Brand, a basketball magazine from the Bahamas.
As an eighth-grader, Buddy Hield was rated by the All Bahamian Brand as the best eighth-grader in the Bahamas and one to watch.

Buddy Hield showed his early ability to lead his team from a young age by taking his Jack Hayward basketball team to the championship of the Providence Holiday Tournament on a buzzer-beater and also leading his team to win the Grand Bahamas High School Championships.
For his exploits, Buddy Hield was named an All Bahamian Brand All Bahamian Selection.
Buddy Hield was recruited to attend Sunrise Christian Academy in Bel Aire, a basketball prep school in a suburb of Wichita, Kansas.
Former Wichita State assistant and then-Sunrise coach Kyle Lindsted recruited the 6-foot 4-inch (1.93 m) guard.
In 2011, during Buddy Hield's junior year at Sunrise Christian, he led the team to the National Association of Christian Athletes national championship, getting named the MVP of the tourney.
In the 2011–2012 season, his senior year, Buddy Hield averaged 22.7 points on .491 shooting in 21.0 minutes per game.
Buddy Hield was highly recruited and selected the Oklahoma Sooners over the Kansas Jayhawks.
As a freshman at Oklahoma, Buddy Hield scored 7.8 points per game.
Buddy Hield was the recipient of the team's Most Inspirational Award as a freshman at Oklahoma.
Buddy Hield was a second-team All-Big 12 selection as a sophomore at Oklahoma as he averaged 16.5 points, 4.4 rebounds and 1.4 steals per game.
Prior to his junior year at Oklahoma, Buddy Hield worked on his defense and expanded his offensive game to more of a high-volume three-point shooter.
Buddy Hield averaged 17.4 points and 5.4 rebounds per game as a junior at Oklahoma and shot 41 percent from the field.
Buddy Hield led Oklahoma to a 24–11 record and Sweet 16 berth as a junior at Oklahoma.
Despite being a potential 2015 NBA draft selection, Buddy Hield decided to return for his senior season at Oklahoma.
Buddy Hield was a First Team All-Big 12 selection and was named Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year in his senior year at Oklahoma.
Buddy Hield was listed on the Oscar Robertson Award preseason watchlist as well as the Naismith College Player of the Year preseason watchlist.

On January 4, 2016, Buddy Hield recorded a career high of 46 points in a triple overtime loss to Kansas, receiving a standing ovation from the opposing crowd after a postgame interview with Scott Van Pelt.
His 46 points tied the record for most points scored by an opponent at Allen Fieldhouse.
Buddy Hield was named to the 35-man midseason watchlist for the Naismith Trophy on February 11, 2016.

On April 7, 2016, Buddy Hield won the John R. Wooden Award as the best college basketball player for the 2015–16 season, in which he averaged 25 points, 5.7 rebounds, two assists per game, and led the nation in three-point shots.
On June 23, 2016, Buddy Hield was selected by the New Orleans Pelicans with the sixth overall pick in the 2016 NBA draft.
On July 22, 2016, Buddy Hield signed with the Pelicans.
On December 15, 2016, Buddy Hield had his best outing as a Pelican with 21 points and five three-pointers in a 102–95 win over the Indiana Pacers.
On January 3, 2017, Buddy Hield was named Western Conference Rookie of the Month for December.

On February 20, 2017, Buddy Hield was traded, along with Tyreke Evans, Langston Galloway and 2017 first-round and second-round draft picks, to the Sacramento Kings for DeMarcus Cousins and Omri Casspi.
Buddy Hield made his debut for the Kings three days later, scoring 16 points off the bench in a 116–100 win over the Denver Nuggets.
On December 15, 2017, Buddy Hield set a new career high with 30 points in a 129–104 win over the Phoenix Suns.
At the season's end, Buddy Hield was named to the NBA All-Rookie First Team.
Buddy Hield began the 2017–18 season as a starter before switching to a bench role and becoming the team's sixth man after seven games.
On November 25, 2017, Buddy Hield scored a season-high 27 points off the bench with a career-high seven 3-pointers in a 97–95 loss to the Los Angeles Clippers.
Buddy Hield shot 43.1 percent from 3-point range in 2017–18, which placed him ninth in the NBA among qualified players.
In December 2018, Buddy Hield had a seven-game streak with 20 points or more.
On January 5, 2019, Buddy Hield scored 32 points and had a career-high eight 3-pointers in a 127–123 loss to the Warriors.
On January 19, 2019, Buddy Hield made an off-balance, fadeaway 3-pointer just before time expired and scored 35 points in a 103–101 win over the Detroit Pistons.

On March 23, 2019, Buddy Hield had 25 points and the franchise season record for 3-pointers in a 112–103 win over the Suns. He made 7 of 14 shots from beyond the arc, giving him 245 3-pointers for the season and surpassing the mark of 240 set by Peja Stojaković in 2003–04.
In April, Buddy Hield broke Damian Lillard's NBA record (599) for most 3-pointers made in a player's first three seasons.
On October 21, 2019, Buddy Hield signed a four-year contract extension.

On December 26, 2019, Buddy Hield accused coaches and teammates of having "trust issues" after he was benched late in regulation of a game that the Kings eventually lost in double overtime to the Minnesota Timberwolves. He apologized to the entire team the next day for his remarks.

Buddy Hield eventually lost his starting spot to Bogdan Bogdanović, but the switch produced a boost in his production and efficiency; in only his second game off the bench, on January 27, 2020, and again against the Timberwolves, Buddy Hield scored a career-high 42 points to lead the Kings to a 133–129 overtime victory.
Afterwards, Buddy Hield dedicated the game to his idol Kobe Bryant, who died in a helicopter accident the day prior.
On February 15, 2020, Buddy Hield won the Three-Point Contest at NBA All-Star Weekend in Chicago, topping Devin Booker 27–26 in the final round.
On December 23, 2020, Buddy Hield recorded 22 points, four rebounds, and three assists, alongside a game-winning, buzzer-beating tip-in, in a 124–122 overtime win against the Denver Nuggets.
On February 28, 2021, Buddy Hield became the fastest player in NBA history to make 1,000 3-pointers, needing 350 games only to reach the mark.

Before the start of the 2023–24 season, Buddy Hield changed his jersey number for the first time in his career, switching from 24 to 7, formerly worn by Pacers Jermaine O'Neal, Al Jefferson, Malcolm Brogdon, and George Hill.

In back-to-back games coming off the bench, Buddy Hield scored 19 points, once in a one-point loss to the Charlotte Hornets on November 4, and again in a 41–point win against rookie Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs on November 6, giving head coach Rick Carlisle his 900th career win.
On February 8, 2024, Buddy Hield was traded to the Philadelphia 76ers in a three-team deal involving the San Antonio Spurs.
On February 9, 2024, Buddy Hield made his 76ers debut, putting up 20 points and six assists in a 127–121 loss to the Atlanta Hawks.
Buddy Hield played in a league-high total of 84 games in the 2023–24 season, averaging 12.1 points, 3.2 rebounds, and 2.8 assists.

On July 6, 2024, Buddy Hield was traded to the Golden State Warriors in a six-team trade also including the Minnesota Timberwolves, Dallas Mavericks, Denver Nuggets and Charlotte Hornets, which became the NBA's first six-team transaction.

Buddy Hield traveled to the city of Tepic in Nayarit, Mexico from August 1 to 7, 2014 to represent the Bahamas national team in the 2014 Centrobasket, which is the regional basketball championship of FIBA Americas for the Central American and Caribbean subzone.
Buddy Hield's coach in the tournament was Larry Eustachy.
He averaged a tournament-leading 19.8 points per game and a team-high 6.0 rebounds.

In the days after Hurricane Dorian struck the Bahamas, Buddy Hield donated $105,000 to the Hurricane Dorian Relief fund and created a GoFundMe page to help raise an extra $1,000,000 to help families devastated by the hurricane there.
